subject: Thanks for the 2.10 update and the ODE work

messages.author: bacb0402e67daa77
messages.subject: Thanks for the 2.10 update and the ODE work
parts: For once, not a stupid question. I just wanted to thank the whole team for the latest update to Stan. Really digging the syntax update, and I'd in particular like to thanks Sebastian and everybody else who worked on the updated ODE solver. It's already making some things easier for me. Looking forward to what cool things you guys do next!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Thanks for the 2.10 update and the ODE work
parts:
Thanks. We love to get feedback. Let us know if you
have any suggestions for other things that would make your
life easier.

WARNING: You'll need to update to 2.11; there was a subtle
bug in 2.10 that our sampler diagnostics didn't catch and
is patched in 2.11.

We're improving the syntax even more. In 2.12 we will have
compound declare and define and all the unary functions will
be applicable to any container pointwise. At that point, Mitzi
and I are going to rewrite all the example models to bring
them up to date.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Thanks for the 2.10 update and the ODE work
parts:
We aren't going to allow (a + b) for variables declared as:

matrix[M, N] a;
real b[M, N];

a + b; // ***NO!!!***

There's no way to figure out what the result type would
be. We also don't want to mix arrays and matrix operations.
If you want arithmetic, everything should be a matrix or
vector; the arrays are just containers for iterating over.

We will be vectorizing binary functions.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Thanks for the 2.10 update and the ODE work
parts:
I've intentionally limited arithmetic to the int, real,
vector, row_vector, and matrix types. The containers are
really just meant to be used as containers. To do what you
want:

matrix[M, N] a;
matrix[M, N] b;

matrix[M, N] c = a + b;
matrix[M, N] d = a .* b;

- Bob
